etymologies.etymologyHTML: From philosophy +‎ -ical, from Ancient Greek φιλοσοφία (philosophía, “love of knowledge, scientific learning”). Displaced native Old English ūþwitlīċ.

quote.citation: 1846, Edgar Allan Poe, “The Sphinx”, in Arthur's Ladies Magazine:
quote.text: His richly philosophical intellect was not at any time affected by unrealities.

quote.citation: 1911, Hector Hugh Munro, The Schartz-Metterklume Method:
quote.text: She bore the desertion with philosophical indifference.
